name: machine-cleanup
description: Free disk space, memory, and CPU on your computer: find caches tools rebuild, build output git ignores, large and duplicate files, idle projects, unused apps and their leftovers, old tool versions, AI models, and dev servers left running, pick on a local page, and free only your picks, with anything another session uses kept out of reach

interface.longDescription: Scans your macOS, Linux, or WSL machine at the lowest CPU and disk priority, within a time limit, for what takes space and what holds memory and CPU: caches that npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun, pip, uv, Homebrew, Cargo, Go, Gradle, Maven, CocoaPods, Docker, Xcode, and apps rebuild, build output such as node_modules that git ignores, the Trash, old logs and installers, large and duplicate files, git projects nobody has used for 30 days whose commits are all on the remote, apps not opened for 90 days and files that removed apps left behind, tool versions no project uses, models downloaded by Ollama, Hugging Face, and LM Studio, dev servers and watchers left running after their session ended, heavy processes, login items, and running containers. It shows them on a page served only to your browser on this computer, where you pick what to free. Anything a live agent session, an open terminal, or a running program in the same project uses is shown but cannot be picked, and sync folders such as iCloud Drive and Dropbox are never scanned. It frees only your picks: tools clean their own caches with their own commands, your files, apps, and projects move to the Trash, processes get the end signal first, and login items can be turned back on. It reports free disk, memory, and load before and after, measured on the machine. It uses Python, and docker, lsof, and the package managers when they are installed.
defaultPrompt: Find what is filling my disk and let me pick what to free
